method: Read 100 stories from representative batches (1, 5, 10, 15) spanning all 377 unaudited outlines. Scored on 8 dimensions: plot, character, vocabulary, grammar, pacing, emotion, setting, coherence.

plot.issue: Formulaic arcs — problem→struggle→solve→success. No real stakes, tension, or surprise. 'Because of this' connectors make causality feel mechanical.

character.issue: Characters are functional but flat. They 'feel worried' then 'feel proud' with little internal complexity. Heroes rarely make mistakes or have genuine flaws.

vocabulary.issue: Generally appropriate for ESL learners. Good variety per story. This is consistently the strongest dimension across all batches.

grammar.issue: Clean and correct. Sentence structures are varied enough. Minor issue: some run-on compound sentences.

pacing.issue: Most problematic dimension. Beat 1 is always setup, Beats 2-4 are formulaic middle, Beat 5 is always climax, Beat 6 is always resolution. No variation. Stories feel templated.

emotion.issue: Emotions are told not shown. 'She felt proud', 'A wave of relief washed over her'. Limited emotional range — usually anxiety→pride.

setting.issue: Vietnamese settings (Mộc Châu, Da Nang, Phu Quoc etc.) add cultural value. But settings are decoration rather than active story elements.

coherence.issue: Stories are internally consistent but predictable. Beat-to-beat transitions are robotic: 'After that,' 'Because of this,' 'Then,' repeat.

systemicIssues.description: Nearly every beat starts with 'After that,' 'Because of this,' or 'Then,'. Some stories use the same connector 3+ times in 6 beats.
examples: Story #1: 'After that' x3, 'Because of this' x2
Story #12: 'Because of this' x3, 'After that' x2

systemicIssues.description: Almost all stories follow: Beat1=Setup → Beat2=Problem → Beat3=Attempt → Beat4=Progress → Beat5=Success → Beat6=Resolution+moral. No subversion, no ambiguity.
examples: Story #8 (Leo's Banking App), Story #16 (Leo's New Recipe), Story #88 (Leo's Creative Breakthrough) all follow identical arcs

systemicIssues.description: Emotions follow anxiety→determination→pride with little variation. Characters rarely feel conflicted, angry, jealous, or ambivalent.
examples: 'Linh felt worried' → 'Linh felt much more confident' → 'Linh felt proud'

systemicIssues.description: Problems resolve too easily. Characters 'work hard' off-screen and then succeed. The struggle is mentioned but never felt.
examples: Story #98 (Mai in Da Nang): struggles with English → attends classes → immediately succeeds at client presentation

systemicIssues.description: Many stories share near-identical themes: 'Linh improves English', 'character overcomes challenge through hard work', 'teamwork saves the day'. Name variations on the same plot.
examples: Stories #2, #7, #14, #17 are all 'Linh improves English through practice'

systemicIssues.description: Nearly every story ends with an explicit moral lesson ('This story teaches...', 'Linh's journey showed that...'). Breaks immersion and feels preachy.
examples: 'Linh's journey shows that practice and heart can help you overcome challenges.'
'This story shows how teamwork and good habits can help a community overcome challenges'

good.description: Engaging premise, some character depth, varied pacing. Examples: The Onyx Tempest (#193), The Zucchini Bread Experiment (#18), A Summer by the Lake (#84)

adequate.description: Readable, educational, but formulaic. Grammar and vocab are fine. Stories 'work' for ESL but aren't engaging.

mediocre.description: All systemic issues present. Predictable, repetitive transitions, flat characters. Functional but not enjoyable.

poor.description: Multiple critical failures: incoherent beats, extreme formulaicness, or barely any narrative arc. Just a sequence of events.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Fix transition prompts — the old prompt forced 'After that', 'Because of this', 'Then' openers. The improved prompt already addresses this but existing stories need regeneration.
CRITICAL: Regenerate ALL existing cached stories with the improved prompt. The old prompt produced systematically inferior quality.
HIGH: Add plot variety — the prompt should occasionally produce stories where the character fails, where the resolution is bittersweet, or where the 'problem' isn't solved by individual effort.
MEDIUM: Reduce ending moralism — add prompt instruction to end with the story itself, not an explicit lesson.
MEDIUM: Diversify themes — too many 'Linh learns English' stories. Stories should cover wider range of genuine conflicts.
LOW: Add emotional complexity — prompt should encourage showing emotions through actions/dialogue, not just stating them.
